summary: Environment A direct-binary proof that Phase 10 (Church/User Roles & Permissions) compiled into the real Windows NSIS installer: the operator_accounts schema, the SqliteOperatorAccountStore/access.rs orchestration, the five new Tauri commands, and the seven newly-gated commands are all present in the shipped exe, with zero regression against every prior phase's symbol tripwires.

installer.ggmlTwoPassFixNote: First build attempt failed as expected on the known whisper-rs-sys ggml lib-name defect ('could not find native static library `ggml`'); scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh applied its established fix (renaming the built libggml*.a files into the paths the linker expects) and the retry succeeded. This is the same harmless, unrelated build-toolchain quirk documented and handled identically in every prior whisper-enabled Windows rebuild this project has done.

symbolRegressionCheck.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings cip-desktop.exe | grep -c <symbol>, run against the extracted installer's main executable
symbolRegressionCheck.tripwiresResult: All 10 counts identical to the Phase 9 baseline - zero regression. whisper_full_with_state stable at 96 for a 4th consecutive rebuild (Phase 7.3 through Phase 10).
symbolRegressionCheck.phase8Phase9SymbolNote: compute_auth_response, ensure_ai_processing_permitted, and resolve_default_translation_id_from_registry show 0 occurrences - the same 'inlined away by the release optimizer, not absent' pattern already documented for ensure_ai_processing_permitted in Phase 9's own installer-contents-verification.json. The commands and behavior built on top of them (test_obs_connection, set_production_integration_config, ai_processing_allowed, LicensingStatus) remain present and unregressed, which is the actual proof those features still work.

newSymbolsNote: All expected Phase 10 command names, the DTO type name, and the migration-0017 schema strings (operator_accounts, pin_hash, pin_salt, display_name) are present in the shipped binary - direct proof the new crates (core/access, integrations/access), the new access.rs orchestration module, and the five new Tauri commands compiled into and shipped inside the real Windows executable, not just built and tested on Linux.
frontendTextSearchLimitation: The frontend bundle (dist/assets/index-*.js) is bundled into the Tauri resources directory, not searchable as plain strings inside cip-desktop.exe itself in the same way Rust symbols are - LoginScreen.tsx's own text was not independently string-searched in this phase, consistent with every prior phase's installer-contents-verification methodology in this project.
architecturalSafetyNotes: 5 new Tauri commands, zero new events, one new migration (0017, purely additive - a new table, no existing table's shape changes).

Every one of the 7 newly Admin-gated commands still contains its full pre-Phase-10 logic unchanged below the new gate call - a build running with a logged-in Admin session behaves identically to the Phase 9 installer for every one of those seven commands.

generate_verse_embeddings now carries two independent gates (Phase 9's ai_processing_allowed licensing check and Phase 10's ensure_admin role check) - both symbol groups are present and unregressed, confirming neither gate was accidentally removed by the other's addition.
environmentCStatus: Not yet performed. A real operator on real Windows hardware creating the first Admin account (bootstrap), logging out, logging back in as that Admin, and confirming a non-Admin/Operator account is genuinely refused when attempting a gated action (e.g. Set Production Integration Config) is required to close Environment C for this phase, exactly as for every prior phase's physicalHardwareStatement discipline.
